item.content:encoded:
This is an interesting one, its just this method of expunging/redacting in all these articles grates on me, I know its an authorial decision plus the articles old, but if you're gonna stick with this thing (and there's no reason you shouldn't, its a personal style choice and doesnt by itself decide my vote, although in one that was in the balance, it could lean me to a downvote) wouldn't a blackbox make more sense for believeability? I can buy a lazy censor with a black marker, but not a lazy censor who types out a couple of letters and then [REDACTS], as it's actually more work to do this than just redact the correct word.
It's a suspension of disbelief thing, if a minor one.
+1, despite the annoying way you handle redaction.

item.content:encoded: IIRC, it's a sort of an author's thumbprint by making it look like it was transcribed from a paper copy. Sometimes, with real documents before Microsoft Word was around, words and sentences could get clipped off at the end of a page and start on a new one. If you're quickly censoring a document, you can miss the fact that the last bit of what you're removing is on the next page.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
People like to ask me about the cutting into words thing. Yes, I do it on purpose.

See, most users here write a certain doctor or researcher or agent, and call it their character, and use them in a lot of writing and tales and et cetera. Not so with me; I make up names as I go, except for renfield, who's more or less my kenny. No. I go for something a bit more subtle. See, my recurring "character" on the wiki is a censor. Particularly, a distinctively lazy censor who tends to be sloppy with the editing, and has a habit of missing bits of what he's supposed to be removing.

And now you know.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It does make the article seem unpolished that both [EXPUNGED] and [REDACTED] are used for enjambment.

It seem to remember that the recent trend is to use data expunged in this fashion for information that's been corrupted and redacted for stuff that's been taken out intentionally. Of course, there is no canon.

I just find the use of the mid-word redaction / expungment to be kind of passe already. The frequency of use in this article only increases the feeling for me. The second redacted could easily be changed to the word 'details.' with nothing lost from the article, in my opinion.

The third redacted gives me the impression that you used it because it was safer than coming up with an estimate of how long the head would take to decay which might be questioned. Unless I'm missing the implication with the third redacted, it's kind of unnecessary.

Also, based on Enma Ai's comment about Psi-8, the only conclusion I can draw is that it didn't get out via grave-to-surface travel.

item.content:encoded:
Psi-8 is the MTF that "find all forms of communication between graves and the surface, normally put into place as a precaution against accidental burial, such as pipes, bells, and even phones, and sever them".

I'd guess that if heads suddenly removed themselves from dead bodies and started to act like crabs, these guys would find out about it first. Their involvement probably means that the Foundation suspects that more instances of 565 can be created from dead bodies buried in cemeteries.

I like this one, although I can't help but think that it'd be creepier if acted more like a jellyfish instead of a crab. Imagining this thing moving by crawling near the ground makes it look kinda silly; if it was just a slowly floating head with a bunch of brain-tentacles dragging behind it… brr.
